stories.summary: To understand how societies might react to climate change, archaeologists look at social responses to extreme climate events in the past—and in some places, that included measures as drastic as human sacrifice. Mass ritual sacrifices along the desert coast of northern Peru have been linked to catastrophic flooding caused by El Niño, which made researchers wonder if such sacrifices were part of a rise in violence driven by resource scarcity. But a new survey of the Lambayeque Valley suggests that violence was extremely rare, even during periods of ecological upheaval.

stories.title: Kicking Controversy Continues With Another Miss From Butker
stories.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs gave kicker Harrison Butker another chance, but it didn't go as well as they'd planned. Butker's latest miss occurred just before halftime when the Chiefs' win over hte New York Jets was still a close game. The miss came from 51 yards out as the ball sailed wide right. The kicker made all five of his extra points, but that was small consolation given the severity of the problem going into this game. The kicker was booed by fans, but he didn't slam them, saying "I'm booing myself sometimes," per a report from Nate Taylor of ESPN. He knows fans are passionate and want to win games, then added "I've got to be better."
